newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy budget to raise no less than 37trln lire-PDS.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget to raise no less than 37trln lire-PDS.

text.p: The 1997 budget, which was due to cut 34.2 trillion lire off next year's deficit, will now have to be more incisive than originally planned, the parliamentary party leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) said.
"By now the 37 trillion lire threshold is obligatory because accounts have worsened and there's the labour pact to pay for," said Fabio Mussi, PDS leader in the lower house of parliament.
The PDS is the largest single party within the government coalition. The budget is due to be unveiled on Friday.
The government on Monday signed a labour pact with unions and employers in which it pledged to set aside 14 trillion lire over the next three years for projects to boost jobs.
The Treasury wants to raise 3.5 trillion lire of this with the forthcoming budget.
Sources close to one Italian ministry said the 1997 budget would look to cut 38.5 trillion lire off the deficit.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi is due to meet government allies later on Thursday to discuss the budget package, with the hard-left Communist Refoundation refusing Treasury demands for cuts to pensions and health spending.
"Nothing can be ruled out," Mussi told reporters. "Certainly in a coalition, the budget isn't something which just a single party calls for," he added. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
